stem.en: A slice of potato is left in strong salt solution and shrinks. What caused this?

text.en: Salt moved into the potato and pushed its contents out.

feedback.en: Salt is not what moved here. Think about water.

text.en: Net movement of water out of the cells, towards more solute.

feedback.en: Yes. Water crosses both ways, and more of it leaves.

text.en: Water stopped crossing the membrane in both directions.

feedback.en: Water goes on crossing. The net movement is outwards.

text.en: The cell walls of the potato dissolved in the salt solution.

feedback.en: Salt solution does not dissolve the cell walls.

explanation.en: Water crosses the membrane both ways. With more solute outside, more water leaves than enters, so the potato shrinks.

hints.en: Which substance moves through the membrane?
